tasks.short: Train and supervise museum staff and volunteers

steps.what: Prepare collection-specific training material
Train, observe and supervise people handling collection work
Record actual training and individual follow-up needs

tasks.design: Reuse headings and approved illustrations in {DOCS} for actual training preparation. Keep live supervision and the separate {LMS} record with the curator; a template cannot establish competence or create observations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Training materials are often reformatted for each intake.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document templates can reuse structure without generating collection-handling advice.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising unsafe handling and judging a trainee's readiness.
tasks.human_edge: Observe the person and adapt explanation to the object and skill gap.
tasks.altitude: Spend a little less preparation time on page layout; supervision rights stay the same.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native document templates reuse layout; supervision and competence assessment remain human.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual preparation, supervision and assigned training records; shares are provisional, not observed measurements.

The curator supplies trainee needs and current approved procedures. s2 produces the observations, person identifier, training date and follow-up facts entered manually in s3; missing facts remain unresolved.

Native preparation templates are tested first. Only two preparation points are removed; the current compact training form already avoids duplicate entry. Its ordinary save remains in s3 without an approval stage.
If this assignment consists only of supervision, remove and reweight the preparation step before estimating benefit.
unknowns: Frequency of actual material preparation versus direct supervision
research_questions: Does a reused collection-specific document remove repeated layout work?

incremental.description: Maintain current template illustrations and headings

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 10 times 20%=2, less 0.5 upkeep gives 1.5. With a new conservation procedure, content and illustrations are rebuilt; only 0.7 point of heading placement is reusable, leaving 0.2 net. All supervision and record writing remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Confer with the board on policies, budgets and operations

steps.what: Verify collection needs, policy issues and budget figures
Assemble checked figures and papers into the board pack
Confer with directors and capture actual decisions and unresolved issues
Write the curator's assigned policy and action record

loop.purpose: Restate captured actions without inventing agreement
loop.check: Curator checks decisions, dissent, conditions and omissions against notes
loop.stop: Missing attribution or two failed drafts returns writing to the curator
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed action table is tried first; irregular discussion needs limited prose restatement

steps.what: Check the complete record and save it in the existing folder

tasks.design: First test a native board-pack template in {DOCS}, then assemble compatible checked figures and linked papers without rewriting policy. A bounded restatement of the curator's captured actions supports the separate record, while board deliberation and the complete record check remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Pack assembly and restating action notes consume manual effort alongside deliberation.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic document assembly and bounded source-based prose restatement.
tasks.still_hard: Trade-offs between collection care, access, policy and available funds.
tasks.human_edge: Represent collection needs accurately and recognise what the board actually agreed.
tasks.altitude: Less document assembly; no additional budget or policy authority.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: document assembly can place checked data and papers; source-based language drafting still needs a meaning check.

assumptions: Shares describe curator labour only, not directors' meeting time. Actual assigned action writing is included; no new board secretariat duty is assumed.

s1 produces checked period, account, amount, currency and paper references from finance-owned records, with manual verification for missing exports. s3 captures actual decisions, owners and dates; unknown owners or dates are left open.
Try native pack assembly before custom glue. Full source verification, conversation and final checking remain; the internal save is ordinary author work without a gate.
No distribution or formal policy enactment is included in this confer-and-record boundary; if assigned, each actual send or enactment needs its own final-version gate.
unknowns: Compatibility of finance exports with the board-pack layout
Whether the curator or a separate secretary owns the action record
research_questions: Which board-pack elements are repeated placement rather than policy analysis?

incremental.description: Maintain pack mappings and check restatement behaviour

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 10 assembly plus 2 restatement points=12, less 1 upkeep gives 11. With incompatible fiscal periods and disputed policy wording, retain most assembly and all substantive drafting: only 2 points of compatible paper placement and 0.5 of action restatement disappear, giving 1.5 net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Verify object schedules, values, loan conditions and existing coverage
Determine coverage needs and prepare the object schedule
Prepare the broker request from the checked schedule
Check the exact broker request, attachments and recipient
Send the authorised request to the broker
Assess returned terms and recommend collection coverage changes
Check final coverage instructions against delegated authority and save the recommendation
Send the exact authorised coverage instruction

tasks.design: Use an {EMAIL} request template fed by a curator-checked object schedule from the collection module in {OPS_SYSTEM}. Keep coverage interpretation and recommendations human, and retain separate final-version gates on both the broker request and any authorised coverage instruction.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated request headings and attachment lists are prepared manually.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing mail templates can reuse the request structure.
tasks.still_hard: Valuation, exclusions, transit terms and whether delegated authority permits binding coverage.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when seemingly similar policies leave a particular object or journey uncovered.
tasks.altitude: Less request formatting, with existing coverage authority unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: mail templates can reuse request structure; insurance scope and binding instructions require human interpretation.

assumptions: All shares are provisional curator labour, not a measured baseline. Actual insurance arrangement and written recommendations are included.

Collection staff produce object identifiers, descriptions, valuations and lender terms; s1 verifies them and s2 supplies the request schedule. Missing values require manual follow-up, never estimates from a model. The broker produces returned terms after s5; broker labour is outside the focal denominator and is not claimed as saved.
Try native mail templates first. Only request structure loses time; capture, schedule preparation, complete checks, recommendations, ordinary saves and both real sends are retained.

This scenario assumes the curator has delegated authority for the final instruction. Otherwise add the actual budget-holder decision and its labour before s8; do not treat a recommendation as authority to bind.
Changes after either check void that action's approval.
unknowns: Whether object schedules already populate request attachments
research_questions: Does the current broker request require repeated formatting or only a short existing template?

incremental.description: Keep broker request headings and attachment requirements current

approvals.approved_version: s3 final broker request with exact object schedule and recipient checked in s4; edits void approval
s7 final coverage instruction with exact terms and broker recipient; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only 15 times 20%=3 request-formatting points disappear, less 0.6 upkeep gives 2.4. A bespoke international loan needs rewritten requirements and attachments, leaving just 0.8 point of reusable request headings, or 0.2 net. Neither send nor ordinary save earns savings.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Establish event needs, capacity and fee rules
Coordinate actual entertainment, refreshments and decorations with providers
Enter event timing, resources and setup tasks
Prepare and check the final provider booking
Send the authorised provider booking
Check actual event setup and handle on-site details
Collect assigned event fees and establish actual payment facts
Record and reconcile actual event fee receipts

tasks.design: Use native event templates in {PROJECT} and {CALENDAR} for recurring setup tasks, retaining actual provider coordination and a gated final booking send. Use event and fee defaults in the admissions module of {OPS_SYSTEM} for the separate receipt record, keeping actual collection and reconciliation human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated setup tasks and stable event references are entered again.
tasks.enabler_now: Native task templates and admissions defaults can supply repeated fields.
tasks.still_hard: Provider availability, actual setup problems and disputed payments.
tasks.human_edge: Coordinate providers and resolve visitor or event exceptions in context.
tasks.altitude: A little less repeated setup entry; event decisions and financial responsibility stay unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: event task templates and admissions defaults can reuse stable fields without establishing availability or actual receipts.

assumptions: Provisional shares describe a curator who actually organises events and collects assigned fees. Remove and reweight fees where admissions staff own them; no saving from transferred staff labour.

s1 establishes event identifier, capacity and authorised fee rules. s2 supplies agreed times and resource needs manually; s7 produces actual amount, payment reference and event association for s8. Missing payment facts require manual resolution.
Test native task templates and event defaults first. The cuts remove repeated task setup and event-reference entry only, not negotiations, payments, reconciliation, saves or sends.
A native receipt created with the payment is existing runtime and earns no saving; if it already removes s8 entry, remove that baseline before estimating benefit.
s4 includes the complete booking, provider, price and destination; changes void its approval. Provider performance is not counted as curator time.
unknowns: Actual division between curator and admissions team
Whether receipt records already inherit event references
research_questions: Which recurring setup fields and receipt references does the curator still enter manually?

incremental.description: Maintain event task and fee defaults

approvals.approved_version: s4 final booking with exact provider, terms and recipient; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 15 times 20% plus 14 times 10%=4.4, less 0.7 upkeep gives 3.7. At an unfamiliar venue with variable fees, only 0.8 point of reusable schedule headings and 0.4 of event-reference entry remain removable, giving 0.5 net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Keep collection, staff and visitor decisions; reduce repeated document and event entry.
skills_to_grow: Check coverage requests against object schedules
Measure actual admissions entry before changing it
role.ambitious_version: Use reclaimed preparation time for collection-specific explanations and closer event follow-up, subject to observed savings.
